title: A normalized derived comparison on a common augmented resolution
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal D$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ having enough injectives (every object is a subobject of an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions]). Use bounded-below cochain complexes and their localizations $Q$ at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Let $U:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$, $E:\mathcal A\to\mathcal D$, and $H:\mathcal B\to\mathcal D$ be additive functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Fix their bounded-below right derived functors and natural comparison maps $\alpha^U_J:Q(UJ)\to RU(QJ)$, $\alpha^E_I:Q(EI)\to RE(QI)$, $\alpha^H_J:Q(HJ)\to RH(QJ)$, with the canonical injective computations of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. Let $\sigma:EU\xrightarrow{\sim}H$ be a natural isomorphism. Suppose a natural isomorphism $b:RE\circ RU\xrightarrow{\sim}RH$ is given, normalized for every bounded-below injective complex $J$ for which $UJ$ is termwise injective by
$$b_{QJ}\circ RE(\alpha^U_J)\circ\alpha^E_{UJ}=\alpha^H_J\circ Q(\sigma_J).$$
Here $\sigma_J$ is its termwise chain isomorphism.

Let $M\in\mathcal A$, $N\in\mathcal B$, and let $h:N[0]\to J$ be a bounded-below injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Suppose $I=UJ$ is termwise injective and $a:M[0]\to I$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Put
$$e=RU(Qh)^{-1}\circ\alpha^U_J:QI\xrightarrow{\sim}RU(N[0]),\qquad \eta=e\circ Qa.$$
Define the canonical computation isomorphisms
$$c^E_a=(\alpha^E_I)^{-1}\circ RE(Qa),\qquad c^H_h=(\alpha^H_J)^{-1}\circ RH(Qh).$$
Then the specified morphism $c=b_{N[0]}\circ RE(\eta)$ satisfies the equality in $D^+(\mathcal D)$
$$c^H_h\circ c=Q(\sigma_J)\circ c^E_a.$$
Thus its chain representative, using exactly $a$ and $h$, is $\sigma_J$, in particular the identity when $EU=H$ and $\sigma$ is the identity.

These computations are natural in maps of the augmented data: if $f:M\to M'$, $g:N\to N'$ and $t:J\to J'$ obey $t h=h'g$ and $U(t)a=a'f$, then
$$c^E_{a'}\circ RE(f)=Q(EU(t))\circ c^E_a,\qquad c^H_{h'}\circ RH(g)=Q(H(t))\circ c^H_h,$$
and $Q(H(t))Q(\sigma_J)=Q(\sigma_{J'})Q(EU(t))$. All assertions are equalities of derived morphisms, not only of individual cohomology groups.

proof.text: First justify the inverses, without imposing exactness on $U,E,H$. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] to $U$ and $H$ on the bounded-below injective complex $J$ in $\mathcal B$, and to $E$ on the bounded-below injective complex $I=UJ$ in $\mathcal A$. The source categories have enough injectives by hypothesis, so $\alpha^U_J$, $\alpha^H_J$, and $\alpha^E_I$ are isomorphisms. Since $h$ and $a$ are quasi-isomorphisms, the localization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] makes $Qh$ and $Qa$ invertible. Functors preserve inverses by applying them to the two inverse identities. Thus $RU(Qh)$, $RH(Qh)$ and $RE(Qa)$ are invertible, as are $e,\eta,c^E_a,c^H_h$. In the remaining steps write $q=Qh$, $x=Qa$, and $A_U=\alpha^U_J$, $A_E=\alpha^E_I$, $A_H=\alpha^H_J$; composition is read right to left.

source.place: Tags 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic), 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived), 05SA (lemma-derived-functor); agent-written calculation for the stipulated normalization.

proof.text:
Apply the assumed naturality of $b:RE\circ RU\to RH$ to $q:Q(N[0])\to QJ$. It gives $RH(q)\circ b_{N[0]}=b_{QJ}\circ RE(RU(q))$. Substitute $\eta=RU(q)^{-1}\circ A_U\circ x$ into the definition of $c$ and apply functoriality of $RE$. Cancelling $RE(RU(q))\circ RE(RU(q)^{-1})=1$ yields
$$RH(q)\circ c=b_{QJ}\circ RE(A_U)\circ RE(x).$$
This uses only the stated naturality, functor composition and inverse identities; it does not require $U$ to preserve arbitrary quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic), 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived), 05SA (lemma-derived-functor); agent-written calculation for the stipulated normalization.

proof.text:
The assumed normalization applies to this very $J$ because $J$ is bounded below and injective and $UJ=I$ is termwise injective. Its equation is $b_{QJ}\circ RE(A_U)\circ A_E=A_H\circ Q(\sigma_J)$. Compose on the right with $A_E^{-1}\circ RE(x)$ to obtain
$$b_{QJ}\circ RE(A_U)\circ RE(x)=A_H\circ Q(\sigma_J)\circ A_E^{-1}\circ RE(x).$$
Combining with step 2 and then composing on the left with $A_H^{-1}$ gives
$$c^H_h\circ c=A_H^{-1}\circ RH(q)\circ c=Q(\sigma_J)\circ A_E^{-1}\circ RE(x)=Q(\sigma_J)\circ c^E_a.$$
This is the required equality in $D^+(\mathcal D)$. Since $c^E_a$ and $c^H_h$ are exactly the specified computation isomorphisms, it also gives the specified chain representative $\sigma_J$. If $EU=H$ and $\sigma$ is the identity, its image is the identity.

proof.text:
For a map $(f,g,t)$ of augmented data as in the statement, let $I'=UJ'$, $s=U(t):I\to I'$, and $A'_E=\alpha^E_{I'}$. Write $RE(f)$ for $RE(Q(f[0]))$. Naturality of the given comparison $\alpha^E$ says $RE(Qs)\circ A_E=A'_E\circ Q(E(s))$, so $ (A'_E)^{-1}\circ RE(Qs)=Q(E(s))\circ A_E^{-1}$. The augmentation identity $s\circ a=a'\circ f[0]$ now gives
$$c^E_{a'}\circ RE(f)=(A'_E)^{-1}\circ RE(Q(a'\circ f[0]))=(A'_E)^{-1}\circ RE(Qs)\circ RE(Qa)=Q(EU(t))\circ c^E_a.$$
Only naturality and the stated augmentation identity are used; no choice of a chain lift is made.

source.place: Tags 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic), 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived), 05SA (lemma-derived-functor); agent-written calculation for the stipulated normalization.

proof.text:
Put $A'_H=\alpha^H_{J'}$ and write $RH(g)=RH(Q(g[0]))$. Naturality of $\alpha^H$ gives $(A'_H)^{-1}\circ RH(Qt)=Q(H(t))\circ A_H^{-1}$. Using the other augmentation identity $t\circ h=h'\circ g[0]$ gives
$$c^H_{h'}\circ RH(g)=(A'_H)^{-1}\circ RH(Q(h'\circ g[0]))=(A'_H)^{-1}\circ RH(Qt)\circ RH(Qh)=Q(H(t))\circ c^H_h.$$
Finally, naturality of $\sigma:EU\to H$ in every degree of $t$ is the chain-map equality $H(t)\circ\sigma_J=\sigma_{J'}\circ EU(t)$. Applying the functor $Q$ gives exactly $Q(H(t))Q(\sigma_J)=Q(\sigma_{J'})Q(EU(t))$. All three naturality equations therefore hold already for derived morphisms, before applying cohomology.
